Known in the market as a specialist for PC components and computer peripherals, we attach great importance to first-class availability of the latest products, fast processing, personal contact and competitive prices. At its headquarters in Dachau and its branches in Eging am See, Braunschweig and Taipei (Taiwan), the wholesaler employs around 180 people from a wide variety of countries. evidence.excerpt: 1.00 EUR = 1.1535 USD * [kontakt@ecom-trading.de](mailto:kontakt@ecom-trading.de) * [+49 8131 / 5695 - 0](tel:+49813156950) * [Email schreiben](mailto:kontakt@ecom-trading.de) * [Jetzt anrufen](tel:+49813156950) * [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/EcomElectronicComponentsTradingGmbh) * [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ecom_trading_gmbh) * [Google](https://g.page/r/CcRrW9WXKLMaEAE) * [XING](https://www.xing.com/companies/ecomelectroniccomponentstradinggmbh) * [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/ecom-electronic-components-trading-gmbh) * [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@ecom_trading_gmbh?_t=8kTfqGyunzM&_r=1) * [de](https://www.ecom-trading.de/news/ecom-wachst-um-15) [ECOM Trading GmbH](https://www.ecom-trading.de/en) # Review of a great fiscal year 2013/14 * [ECOM Electronic Components Trading GmbH](https://www.ecom-trading.de/en) * [News](https://www.ecom-trading.de/en/news) * Ecom achieves a growth of 15 % **Munich/ Eging am See, 12th September 2014**. The ECOM Holding can look back on a great fiscal year: the ECOM Group with its 120 employees could achieve a 15% increase in total sales to more than 250 million euros. In addition to the high revenue ECOM Trading, which is specialized in trading with components, also the own brands NEXOC. and CAPTIVA could contribute a lot to the enormous growth. “The above average performance in the previous fiscal year is also remarkable compared with other companies of the sector”, sums up the managing director Gerhard Ellinger the annual figures of the ECOM Group. The Group is a constant and reliable partner in the German and European component market since 1992. He explicitly emphasizes that particularly these characteristics have been very important to achieve such a successful and sustainable growth. Despite the continued competitive pressure within the distribution, ECOM could strengthen and even expand its market position considerably, also due to the commitment and engagement of its employees. Gerhard Ellinger underlines further that all could be achieved without additional purchases, but with organic growth. The decisive factors for success in the component business, based at the ECOM Trading GmbH, are especially the focus on core product groups, the expansion of the assortment, the excellent availability as well as the good prices and the personal customer care. The own brands with their respective specification and the perfect positioning of the products have also contributed a lot to the successful fiscal year: NEXOC. with its premium and individual notebooks as well as CAPTIVA with its tablets, which have an attractive price-performance ratio, and its individual configurable BTO-PCs across the whole price range. ECOM Manager Gerhard Ellinger defines as the primary goals for the current fiscal year especially the expansion of the existing partnerships with the specialized trade, the intention to convince new customers of the performance of ECOM and its own brands NEXOC. Notebook and Captiva as well as the continued advancement of the assortment und the own product line to develop further the sustainable and organic growth.

findings.statement: The candidate is ECOM Electronic Components Trading GmbH, headquartered at Siemensstr. 9, 85221 Dachau, Germany, registered at District Court of Munich HRB 103935.
notes: Multiple independent and official sources confirm the legal name and German registration.

findings.statement: ECOM operates in Germany with headquarters in Dachau and additional German locations including Eging am See and Braunschweig.
notes: Explicit German addresses and location listings across multiple sources.

findings.statement: The official company website is https://www.ecom-trading.de/, owned by ECOM Trading GmbH, which provides company, product, and contact information.
notes: Domain appears as the official site on the company's own pages, LinkedIn, pressebox, and D&B listing. The submitted ecom-edv.de domain is not evidenced.
Non-standard finding kind "official-website" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: ECOM actively engages with the IT channel ecosystem, including participation in events such as IFA Reseller Park and maintaining a digital presence for channel partners.
notes: LinkedIn company page mentions IFA Reseller Park participation and targeting the DACH market and international business.

findings.statement: ECOM acts as an IT wholesaler/distributor supplying PC components and peripherals to specialist IT retailers, etailers, system builders, and resellers.
notes: Company website explicitly states 'one of the most successful distributors of PC components and accessories in Europe' serving over 12,000 customers. Bloomberg and D&B classify as wholesale distribution.
Non-standard finding kind "distributor-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: ECOM sells IT products to resellers and also markets directly to specialist retailers and etailers, indicating a reseller/wholesale supply relationship.
notes: Language around supplying 'large IT companies through to small and medium-sized retailers' and D&B classification as merchant wholesaler supports downstream reseller supply.
Non-standard finding kind "reseller-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: ECOM operates an online shop and catalog, supporting an e-tailer channel role.
notes: Website contains shop sections and product catalog. E-tailer role is inferred from the active online sales presence; no direct D2C-only evidence found.
Non-standard finding kind "etailer-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: ECOM maintains brand relationships and own brands including NEXOC. and CAPTIVA, and is listed as a channel partner by GIGAIPC.
notes: ECOM's own news page references NEXOC. and CAPTIVA as own brands. GIGAIPC lists ECOM as a local channel partner in Germany.
Non-standard finding kind "brand-relationships" was normalized to brand-relationship.

findings.statement: ECOM employs around 180 people and operates multiple locations including a 10,000 sq.m logistics center in Dachau.
notes: Consistent employee figures across official site and LinkedIn. Ampliz listing of 0-10 employees is contradictory/outdated but minority source.

findings.statement: ECOM achieved over 250 million euros in total sales in fiscal 2013/14 and continues to grow in the distribution market.
notes: Official press release on company website confirms historical revenue and competitive position in distribution. No current revenue figures supplied in evidence.

reasons: Official company website and multiple independent sources (Bloomberg, D&B, LinkedIn, North Data) consistently describe ECOM as an IT wholesaler/distributor.
The defining distributor action—supplying downstream resellers, system builders, and specialist retailers—is explicitly evidenced.
Company owns a dedicated logistics center and maintains upstream brand/vendor relationships, consistent with distribution.
warnings: Submitted domain ecom-edv.de was not corroborated; resolved official domain is ecom-trading.de.
Ampliz listed employee count of 0-10, conflicting with other sources' ~180 employees; treated as minority/outdated.

Formed in 2021 through the merger of SYNNEX and Tech Data, the company sits between major hardware, software, cloud, and infrastructure vendors on one side and resellers, managed service providers, systems integrators, retailers, and other channel partners on the other. Its portfolio spans endpoint devices, servers and storage, networking, cybersecurity, software, cloud subscriptions, AI-related offerings, financing, configuration, logistics, and lifecycle services. The strategic logic is scale plus specialization: TD SYNNEX uses global reach, vendor relationships, credit capabilities, and fulfillment infrastructure to move very high transaction volumes efficiently, while shifting mix toward higher-growth and higher-margin areas such as cloud, security, data, and AI. The company is headquartered in Clearwater, Florida and Fremont, California, serves customers across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific/Japan, and reported roughly $58.4 billion of revenue in fiscal 2024, ended November 30, 2024. TD SYNNEX Delivers Arista Networks Portfolio Across Europe # TD SYNNEX delivers Arista Networks portfolio across Europe ![TD SYNNEX delivers Arista Networks portfolio across Europe](/sites/default/files/styles/article_thumbnail/public/article/2026/Fibre-Fiber.jpg?itok=lJAVHjBU) TD SYNNEX has signed a pan-European distribution deal with Arista Networks. The agreement expands the distributor’s specialised networking portfolio, enabling partners and end customers across Europe to access a broader range of high-performance, next-generation infrastructure solutions. TD SYNNEX will deliver specialist support for partners integrating Arista Networks into their offerings, providing expert guidance in the design, installation, and deployment of complex solutions across the cloud, AI, data centres, cybersecurity, campus networking, and hybrid environments. This will be complemented by comprehensive training and enablement programmes to accelerate partner success, said TD SYNNEX. The deal is actually part of a new global distribution agreement with Arista, and expands on the existing partnership in the European countries of France, Spain, Portugal, and Germany. “Giving our partners access to Arista’s portfolio means they can deliver enterprise-grade networking, automation, and security without complexity. This opens new revenue streams and strengthens our shared commitment to modern, cloud-driven solutions,” said Sam Paris, vice president, security, networking and communications, Europe, TD SYNNEX. Paul Jordan, vice president for EMEA at Arista Networks, added: “We’re broadening the reach of Arista Networks solutions across the IT ecosystem in close collaboration with TD SYNNEX. Their proactive, programmatic partner support and commitment to innovation will help unlock new opportunities and ensure more businesses benefit from our advanced networking portfolio.” Arista Networks delivers a unified networking platform built on Arista EOS (Extensible Operating System), a single, consistent operating system that “powers automation, high availability, deep network visibility, and advanced analytics across the entire infrastructure”, says Arista. correction.primaryChannelReason: Distributor was selected by the role agent from evidence-supported roles; the original search lane was ignored.

findings.statement: The candidate is TD SYNNEX Germany GmbH & Co. OHG, located at Kistlerhofstraße 75, 81379 München, Germany.
notes: Official Kontakt page lists this exact German legal entity and address. Dassault and secunet partner pages also confirm the same entity.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX operates in Germany with multiple offices including Munich, Leinfelden-Echterdingen, and Nettetal.
notes: Official German site and LinkedIn show German locations.

findings.statement: The official German website of TD SYNNEX Germany is https://de.tdsynnex.com/.
notes: Multiple official website pages and partner pages link to de.tdsynnex.com as the German entity's official site.
Non-standard finding kind "official-website" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX is a global IT distributor and solutions aggregator, connecting technology vendors with resellers, VARs, system integrators, and retailers.
notes: Extensive and consistent evidence across official site, LinkedIn, Wikipedia, SEC filings, and M&A profiles confirms global distribution role.
Non-standard finding kind "distributor-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX provides value-added distribution services including technical training, professional services, configuration and integration, and specialist solution portfolios (Advanced Solutions, Datech, Maverick, GCC).
notes: Official services pages and academy content showcase value-added services and specialist portfolios.
Non-standard finding kind "vad-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX serves reseller customers including VARs, corporate resellers, government resellers, and direct marketers.
notes: SEC filing and partner pages describe reseller customers; however this is in the context of distribution, not primary reseller activity.
Non-standard finding kind "reseller-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX offers services such as multi-vendor hardware integration, software imaging, and configuration and integration, supporting a system integrator role.
notes: Official hub and services pages explicitly mention integration and configuration services. IT Europa notes expert guidance in design, installation, and deployment support for partners.
Non-standard finding kind "system-integrator-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX holds distribution and partner agreements with major vendors including Arista Networks, HPE/Aruba, secunet, Dassault Systèmes, HarfangLab, and Iterate.ai.
notes: Multiple vendor partner pages and press releases explicitly name TD SYNNEX as a distributor or distribution partner.
Non-standard finding kind "brand-relationships" was normalized to brand-relationship.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX reported global revenue of $58.4B in fiscal 2024 and record Q4 FY2025 revenue of $17.4B, with a strong global distribution footprint.
notes: IR press release and strategy profiles confirm substantial revenue and distribution scale.

findings.statement: TD SYNNEX has over 23,000 employees globally, with 10,001+ employees indicated on LinkedIn and 25,750 employees according to Unify.
notes: Multiple sources confirm large enterprise size.

reasons: Official German site and multiple independent sources consistently establish TD SYNNEX as a leading IT distributor.
Vendor partner pages from secunet, Arista, Dassault Systèmes, HPE/Aruba, and others explicitly identify TD SYNNEX as a distribution partner.
Value-added services and specialist solution portfolios support VAD/SI roles, but these are ancillary to the core broadline distribution model.
warnings: Submitted company name was 'TD SYNNEX Germany'; official legal entity is 'TD SYNNEX Germany GmbH & Co. OHG'.
Some evidence (SEC filing FDW) is unrelated to TD SYNNEX and was excluded from evidence IDs to avoid contamination.
Deterministic role hints were not auto-added: E-tailer.

The ALSO ecosystem comprises a total potential of more than 140,000 resellers, to whom we offer hardware, software and IT services from more than 800 vendors in over 1,680 product categories. In the spirit of the circular economy, the company provides all services from provision to remanufacturing from a single source. The business activities comprise of the areas of Supply, Solutions and Service. Supply stands for the transactional provisioning of hardware and software. Solutions supports customers in the development of customised IT solutions. evidence.title: ALSO Group - ALSO – The Technology Provider
evidence.excerpt: # ALSO Group ALSO – The Technology Provider IT Services and IT Consulting • Emmen, Kanton Luzern • 90,441 followers • 1,001-5,000 employees ## Overview ALSO Holding AG (ALSN.SW) (Emmen/Switzerland) is Europe’s largest technology provider for the ICT industry, currently active in 31 European countries and in many countries worldwide via PaaS partners. The ALSO ecosystem comprises a total potential of more than 140,000 resellers, to whom we offer hardware, software and IT services from more than 800 vendors in over 1,680 product categories. In the spirit of the circular economy, the company provides all services from provision to remanufacturing from a single source. The business activities comprise of the areas of Supply, Solutions and Service. Supply stands for the transactional provisioning of hardware and software. evidence.title: Herweck DaaS-Manager: Das B2B Mietgeschäft im Überblick
evidence.excerpt: [![Logo der Herweck AG](https://herweck.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/herweck-logo-b.svg)](https://herweck.de) ## Hauptnavigation Presse # Herweck DaaS-Manager ## Device-as-a-Service neu gedacht Mit dem neuen DaaS-Manager bringt Herweck eine Software auf den Markt, die das Mietgeschäft mit IT- und Telekommunikationsgeräten so einfach macht wie Online-Shopping. Revolutionär, simpel und in gleichem Maße komplett. Für Systemhäuser, Reseller und Fachhändler, die ihr Portfolio ohne großen Aufwand erweitern möchten, bedeutet das: Mehr Ertrag, weniger Aufwand – und endlich Schluss mit komplexen Prozessen. **DaaS muss kein Projekt sein – sondern ein Geschäft** DaaS gilt als Zukunftsmodell der IT-Beschaffung. Doch bisher scheitern viele potenzielle Anbieter an komplizierten Prozessen, unübersichtlicher Verwaltung und aufwendigen Kalkulationen. Mit dem Herweck DaaS-Manager ist das Geschichte. Die Plattform bündelt alle Prozesse in einem einzigen digitalen Portal – von der Gerätauswahl über die Angebotserstellung bis hin zur Fakturierung und Lifecycle-Steuerung. „Unser Ziel ist es, mit und für unsere Partner nachhaltige, langfristige und werthaltige Kundenbeziehungen aufzubauen, die planbare Erträge für die Zukunft generieren.", so Hans-Jürgen Witfeld, Teil des Vorstands von Herweck. **Alles in einem Portal – von der Kalkulation bis zur Rückgabe** Der neue DaaS-Manager ist das digitale Herzstück für Reseller und Händler aller Größen, die ihr Geschäftsmodell erweitern möchten. Gerade Händler ohne Vorwissen oder eigene Infrastruktur profitieren von der Möglichkeit, direkt in das Mietgeschäft einzusteigen. Im Portal lassen sich Endkunden verwalten, Angebote kalkulieren, Mietanträge eingeben, Geräte und Umsätze steuern – alles automatisiert, übersichtlich und vollständig digital. Herweck übernimmt im Hintergrund die Logistik und Verwaltung, während der Partner sich auf das Wesentliche konzentriert: Kundenberatung und Wachstum. Auch Endkunden profitieren: Sie erhalten aktuelle Technik ohne Investitionsrisiko, genießen planbare monatliche Kosten und haben jederzeit volle Transparenz über Laufzeiten und Geräte. „Viele Miet- und Abo-Modelle am Markt sind zu komplex. Mit dem Modell von Herweck und dem DaaS-Manager senken wir die Einstiegshürde – und machen das Thema alltagstauglich“, ergänzt Silvie Guardiola, Vertriebsleitung IT-COM bei Herweck. **Whitelabel-ready: Ihre Marke, Ihr DaaS-Shop** Besonders attraktiv: Der DaaS-Manager ist auch als Whitelabel-Lösung verfügbar. Systemhäuser und Händler können den Portalzugang im eigenen Look & Feel gestalten und so ihre Marke in den Vordergrund rücken. Sowohl Händler als auch Endkunden nutzen dieselbe Plattform – vom ersten Angebot bis zur Geräterückgabe. Das vereinfacht nicht nur die Kommunikation, sondern auch das Lifecycle-Management über mehrere Jahre hinweg. **Übersicht trifft Skalierbarkeit** Herweck verfolgt mit dem DaaS-Manager einen klaren Anspruch: Maximale Reduktion bei vollem Funktionsumfang. Die Software ist so konzipiert, dass Partner ihr DaaS-Geschäft schrittweise skalieren können – vom ersten Kunden bis hin zu kompletten Managed-Service-Strukturen. Jörg Herweck bringt es auf den Punkt: „DaaS darf kein Mammutprojekt sein. Es muss sich anfühlen wie ein ganz normales Geschäft – nur smarter.“ **DaaS für alle – weil Einfachheit der Schlüssel ist** Für Systemhäuser und Händler in der Telekommunikationsbranche öffnet der Herweck DaaS-Manager die Tür zu einem neuen Geschäftsmodell. Anstatt sich durch Verträge, Finanzierungsmodelle und Rückgabeprozesse zu kämpfen, können Partner ihren Kunden rundum-sorglos Mietmodelle anbieten – digital, profitabel und zukunftssicher. Sie erhalten so eine Möglichkeit, ihr Angebot zu modernisieren und ohne große Anfangsinvestitionen am boomenden Subscription-Markt teilzuhaben. Mit der Kombination aus intuitiver Bedienung, automatisierten Abläufen und Herwecks etablierter Logistik im Hintergrund schafft der Distributor einen neuen Standard für Device as a Service,

Mit einem **umfassenden Serviceportfolio** helfen wir Ihnen dabei, Abläufe zu vereinfachen, Potentiale besser zu nutzen und **Ihr Geschäft gezielt weiterzuentwickeln**. Unsere **Leistungen verbinden Distribution mit praxisnaher Unterstützung** in Vertrieb, Technik, Marketing und digitalen Tools. Damit Sie effizienter arbeiten, Ihre Kunden professionell betreuen und zusätzliche Ertragschancen erschließen können. * **Unterstützung** bei der **Optimierung** Ihrer Prozesse und **Entlastung** im operativen Tagesgeschäft. * **Stärkung Ihrer Vermarktung** durch praxisnahe Lösungen, Kampagnen und digitale Vertriebstools. * Erschließung **zusätzlicher Umsatz- und Ertragspotenziale** durch neue Geschäftsmodelle. * Self-Service über das **Herweck-Kundencenter** für Belege, Gutschriften und wichtige Vorgänge. * Digitale Lösungen, wie **Aktionsportal**, **Margenrechner** und **DaaS-Manager.** ![](https://herweck.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/0626_Herweck-Web-Relaunch-Bildmaterial_Popart-Elemente_DaaS_neon_RZ.png) ## Device as a Service Mit **Device as a Service (DaaS)** und dem **neuen DaaS-Manager von Herweck** bieten Sie Ihren Geschäftskunden moderne **mobile Business-Endgeräte im Mietmodell** – inklusive Service und mit planbarer monatlicher Rate. Über das **zentrale Portal DaaS-Manager** lassen sich **Angebote kalkulieren**, **Geräte verwalten** und **Prozesse digital steuern**. evidence.excerpt: # Meet Germany's top 30 IT distributors #### Ingram, ALSO and Tech Data dominate but there's no shortage of local heroes in the German distribution market, according to our sister title Channelnomics Did you know that seven cents in every euro spent on ICT in Germany travels through just three giant IT distributors? That's one of the more surprising findings of research into the top 30 ICT distributors in Germany which has been carried out by our sister publication, _Channelnomics.eu_. [You can read Part One of the report in full here](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/feature/2408497/the-top-30-german-it-distributors-you-need-to-know-part-one "You can read Part One of the report in full here"). Undoubtedly one of the German channel's most striking quirks is the extent to which it is bossed by a trio of distribution goliaths in the form of Ingram Micro, Tech Data and ALSO, who boast combined estimated sales of nearly €11bn. Amanuel Dag, DACH country manager at analyst Context, said the power wielded by this triumvirate is closely linked to the market's highly price-sensitive nature. "The market is more consolidated here in Germany and therefore it's more price competitive than other countries," said Dag. "There's not much profit to make. The margins are always lower than one per cent for box-moving business around PCs, tablet and laptops; it's not a big secret that telecoms distributors are making more on laptop bags than the mobile PCs themselves. The saying ‘get big, get niche or get out' counts a lot for distribution in Germany - either they are big enough to survive or they find a niche with a higher margin." But it is perhaps precisely because Swiss ALSO and US broadline duo Tech Data and Ingram dominate so heavily that there exists below them a formidable pack of quirky home-grown heroes that have carved out a niche outside of box-shifting. _Channelnomics.eu_ began its [Focus in Germany season](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/special/2405808/focus-on-germany "Focus in Germany season") by counting down the country's top 50 resellers - or 'system houses'. Stay tuned for Parts Two and Three, which will review 20 to 11, and 10 to one, respectively. evidence.title: Company History
evidence.excerpt: ## Company HistoryInnovation From The Very Beginning. Transfer of our company shares on January 31 to GZS Digital GmbH, a wholly owned subsidiary of Gustav Zech Stiftung. In the course of a BPO (Business Process Outsourcing). project, telent takes over the COLT field service sector. telent arises from the remaining service. ## Portrait. **The telent GmbH is a service provider and telecommunications company based in Backnang. It offers more than 50 years of experience in the area of technology, project planning, installation, commissioning as well as operation and maintenance of communication networks. The company has arisen from Telefunken founded in 1903 and has been based in Backnang since 1954 (AEG Telefunken, ANT Nachrichtentechnik, Bosch Telecom, Marconi).**. Today, telent GmbH offers tailor-made technology solutions and services for the area of mission critical infrastructures, digitalization and industrial plants. For operational and safety-related communication, telent plans, builds up and operates for its customers the necessary network infrastructures composed of most state-of-the-art products and systems from various renowned and well-known manufacturers. These systems guarantee maximum availability and security for all IT equipment and thus for the associated business-critical processes in companies and organizations. When networking and automating digital business processes, telent GmbH focuses on comprehensive experience and competence in the fields of cybersecurity, state-of-the-art IP and operational networks, PMR, IoT, wireless-access (pLTE / 5G) as well as technology and infrastructure service for e-mobility, as an example. The company contributes its know-how to the setup of appropriate IT/OT infrastructures required to implement Smart Energy and Smart Transportation applications more quickly, as well as solutions for both industrial and public sectors in Germany.

evidence.title: telent and Deutsche GigaNetz put 200th PoP site into operation
evidence.excerpt: 4. telent and Deutsche GigaNetz put 200th PoP site into operation. # telent and Deutsche GigaNetz put 200th PoP site into operation. **Backnang, 29.01.2025 - telent GmbH has been working for Deutsche GigaNetz GmbH as a turnkey partner and general contractor for the nationwide fibre optic expansion since 2020 as part of a framework contract. Deutsche GigaNetz is one of the leading telecommunications companies for the roll-out and expansion of fibre optic networks in Germany.**. As part of the broadband expansion projects, telent has developed the entire generic network concept for the PoP sites (Point of Presence) together with Deutsche GigaNetz. As general contractor, telent supplies turnkey PoP sites for these expansion projects with the complete site equipment, including active system technology (Nokia 7360 FX iSAM), and maintains and eliminate these as part of the existing maintenance and service contract. Two different types are used for the PoP locations: A-PoP (Access PoP) as a telecommunications container in various sizes and O-PoP (Outdoor PoP) as a multifunctional housing MFG18. In recent years, telent experts have already set up and equipped around 300 PoP locations for the important nationwide network expansion with future-proof fibre optic technology. In December 2024, the important milestone of connecting the 200th PoP location to Deutsche GigaNetz's fibre optic network was reached in close cooperation. This means that Deutsche GigaNetz customers can reliably use a state-of-the-art, stable fibre optic network with high-speed Internet and high bandwidths. Private customers have been using the energy-efficient GPON technology as part of the MyNet product family right from the start. This provides data rates of between 150 Mbit/s and 2.5 Gbit/s (download). With the ProNet product family, business customers also benefit from high-bit-rate XGS-PON connections with up to 10 Gbit/s (symmetrical). Peter Mertens, telent's general project manager, emphasises the excellent cooperation with the Deutsche GigaNetz project teams involved: "This outstanding performance was only possible thanks to the consistently high level of commitment on both sides in all phases of the project.". telent Key Account Manager Alexander Scharf adds: "telent is pleased to continue the existing successful partnership with Deutsche GigaNetz and, as usual, to be a reliable, competent partner and prime contractor for future expansion projects.".

evidence.title: Network Operators
evidence.excerpt: ## System technology and services fornetwork operators. Network operators are facing constant change. Rapid technological progress (broadband, cloud, IoT, 5G) and the ongoing trend toward networking and digitization of social processes are playing a decisive role in this. In addition to large telecommunications companies and regional and national operators, municipalities, cities, and counties are being called upon to build new infrastructure and provide services. Depending on the required bandwidth, different wired or wireless transmission technologies are used to meet communication requirements. The applications are diverse and range from traditional broadband services to the networking of systems and facilities for future electromobility, smart cities, and intelligent transport systems. As a system integrator, telent combines technologies and systems from different manufacturers to optimally meet individual requirements. ## Quality of living and business spaceBroadband connectivity as a locational advantage. In addition to basic utilities such as water, energy, telecommunications, and public transportation, broadband connectivity is becoming increasingly important for residential areas. Today, good broadband connectivity is a key location advantage that is crucial for retaining and expanding regional and national companies. Especially when setting up branches that need to network with the company headquarters or their customers, an existing broadband connection is an essential criterion for choosing a location. At a time when fast broadband connectivity is becoming a decisive competitive factor, telent offers you customized fiber optic solutions instead of standard solutions. We offer you a strategic partnership and future-proof solutions that not only strengthen the economy, but also sustainably increase the quality of life and attractiveness of your region. High availability, reliability, and cybersecurity are crucial aspects for next-generation communication networks. Continuous network monitoring helps to detect and locate errors and attacks. As a partner company, telent offers such 24-hour support every day of the year. With our Service Competence Center (SCC) and a Managed Network Operations Center (M-NOC), we are available to customers 24/7 for all services in the field of active technology. Juni 2011 # euromicron takes over business operations of telent GmbH Deutschland and initiates the second stage in its corporate strategy as planned euromicron acquired the business operations of telent GmbH Deutschland from Pension Corporation (UK) under an asset deal on June 7, 2011. telent GmbH is a vendor-independent system integrator and technology service provider for communications networks and has a nationwide service team. In the field of system integration, telent GmbH specializes in the technology segments of transmission technology, IP migration, infrastructure, integrated control station technology and professional mobile communications/trunking. It also offers services such as assembly, commissioning and maintenance of technical systems and communications networks. telent GmbH is headquartered in Backnang. Its origins date back to the company Telefunken in 1907 and its current history began in 1954, since when it has been part of AEG Telefunken, Bosch Telecom and Marconi, before being taken over by euromicron. Employing a workforce of around 400, telent GmbH builds and monitors infrastructure for prestigious European carriers, power utilities, large private enterprises and public authorities from the sectors of transport and security. With its extensive technology know-how and a “24-hour Service Competence Center”, the company supports its customers as a partner for complete system solutions at three branch offices and eleven service locations in Germany. The company, which is established in Germany, cooperates with selected partners such as Ericsson, Keymile, Cisco, Motorola, Ceragon and Nexans to offer customers tailored solutions. The existing Managing Directors of telent GmbH, Dr. Stefan Kindt, Robert Blum and Hans-Peter Fischer, will continue to run the company. “With our many years of experience, great technical know-how and motivated employees, we look forward to making a major contribution to the further development of the euromicron Group. Thanks to the new lineup, we can offer our customers an even broader range of services,” stated Dr. Stefan Kindt. The profitable company generates sales in the upper single-digit million range. telent GmbH Deutschland will contribute sales of around €90 million and an EBIT of €6 million to euromicron’s consolidated results as of 2012. euromicron sees interesting potentials and synergies as a result of integration of telent GmbH in the group: * A complementary portfolio of customers, products, service and know-how, etc. * High potential in planning, implementing and maintaining complex networks with various applications * Great technological and problem-solving expertise * Experienced, highly qualified employees * Expansion of the customer base “Takeover of the business operations of telent GmbH Deutschland is of great importance for expanding both parties’ business and will initiate the next stage in euromicron AG’s corporate strategy, which will take the group closer to achieving the 300 million sales mark in 2011,” says Dr. Späth, Chairman of the Executive Board. telent GmbH ([www.telent.de](http://www.telent.de)) is an independent vendor of solutions relating to networks and systems for enterprise and security-related communication. A Wi-Fi site survey is the basis for stable and high-performance Wi-Fi networks in companies. We use professional on-site measurements to identify dead spots, sources of interference, channel overlaps or bottlenecks in data throughput. Thanks to state-of-the-art technology – e.g. Ekahau AI Pro and Sidekick 2 – we analyze the actual Wi-Fi coverage in offices, warehouses or production facilities. We visualize the results in clear heat maps, which serve as a basis for planning and recommendations for optimization. ![Workers during WLAN measurement - Site Survey](https://codemaschine.de/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/arbeiter_bei_messung_mob.webp "arbeiter_bei_messung_mob") ![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20width%3D%27357%27%20height%3D%271000%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%20357%201000%27%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%27357%27%20height%3D%271000%27%20fill-opacity%3D%220%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E) ## Site survey procedure ## Preparation We need the floor plans or building or site plans of the object to be measured in advance. We integrate these into the measurement software. We mainly use the industry-standard EKAHAU AI Pro software. ## Measurement An experienced technician comes to you and systematically measures the Wi-Fi in all relevant areas – using professional equipment (e.g. Ekahau Sidekick 2). Signal strength, channel distribution, interference and other parameters are recorded. ## Report We then prepare all the measurement results in a professional report. You receive heat maps, detailed analyses and clear recommendations for action to optimize your Wi-Fi. ## What we can measure ## Signal Strength (RSSI) Shows how strong the Wi-Fi signal is being received in dBm – just far more precise than any smartphone display. ## Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) The quality of the signal. Indicates how good the signal is compared to the background noise – crucial for stable connections. ## Second Signal Strength (redundancy) For reliability: Should an access point fail, is an alternative signal available? ## Channel Overlaps Wi-Fi is divided into channels in the 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz and 6 GHz bands. Channel overlaps of the same channels lead to a loss of performance. ## Interference Sources The 2.4 GHz band in particular is also used by other devices such as Bluetooth headphones, radios and microwaves. ## Data Throughput With Active Site Survey, we also measure upload and download speeds – how fast can data actually be transferred in the Wi-Fi? ## Site Survey [Get a quote now](https://codemaschine.de/en/contact-us/?service=survey) Our prices depend on the size of the object to be measured – we will be happy to provide you with an individual quote. from €950 for small buildings larger buildings Price on request plus travel and accommodation costs +49 40 / 3 9876 555 [![](https://codemaschine.de/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/logo.png)](https://codemaschine.de/en/) [+49 40 39876555](tel:+494039876555) © 2012 - 2026 - CODE MASCHINE GmbH - [Imprint](/en/imprint/) [Page load link](#) [Go to Top](#)

Unternehmen – Wann sich der Umstieg für KMU lohnt * IT WiFi ![Image 5: WiFi7](blob:http://localhost/3f921161c2e4a983c4626e389493b4ec) WiFi 7 ist da – und verspricht eine Revolution in der drahtlosen Netzwerktechnologie. Mit theoretischen Geschwindigkeiten von bis zu 46 Gbit/s und Latenzen unter 5 Millisekunden klingt der neue Standard nach einem Quantensprung. Doch lohnt sich der Umstieg für Ihr Unternehmen wirklich schon jetzt? Oder ist es klüger, noch zu warten? In diesem Artikel beleuchten wir die technischen Neuerungen, bewerten den praktischen Nutzen für KMU und geben konkrete Empfehlungen für Ihre Investitionsentscheidung. ## Was ist WiFi 7 technisch? WiFi 7, offiziell als IEEE 802.11be mit dem Zusatz **„Extremely High Throughput”** (EHT) bezeichnet, ist die siebte Generation des WLAN-Standards. Die WiFi Alliance hat im Januar 2024 die offizielle Zertifizierung gestartet, und seit Mitte 2025 sind die ersten Enterprise-Access-Points am Markt verfügbar. Der Standard nutzt wie WiFi 6E die drei Frequenzbänder **2,4 GHz, 5 GHz und 6 GHz**, bringt aber entscheidende technische Verbesserungen: ### 320-MHz-Kanäle: Doppelte Bandbreite WiFi 6 nutzt maximal 160-MHz-Kanäle. WiFi 7 verdoppelt diese Bandbreite auf **320 MHz** – allerdings nur im 6-GHz-Band, wo auch entsprechend Platz dafür ist. Diese Verdopplung der Kanalbreite ist vergleichbar mit dem Ausbau einer zweispurigen Autobahn auf vier Spuren: Es können einfach mehr Daten gleichzeitig übertragen werden. Im 5-GHz-Band bleibt es bei 160 MHz, da dort nicht genug Spektrum für breitere Kanäle verfügbar ist. Das 2,4-GHz-Band unterstützt wie bisher maximal 40 MHz. ### 4096-QAM: 20 Prozent mehr Daten pro Übertragung Die **Quadraturamplitudenmodulation** (QAM) bestimmt, wie viele Bits pro Symbol übertragen werden können. WiFi 6 nutzte 1024-QAM mit 10 Bit

öffnet den Netzwerkschrank und steht vor einem Chaos aus Kabeln, bei dem niemand mehr weiß, welches wohin führt. Genau das soll strukturierte Verkabelung verhindern. In diesem Artikel erklären wir Ihnen, was dahintersteckt und warum dieses Konzept für jedes Unternehmen relevant ist. ## Was bedeutet strukturierte Verkabelung? Strukturierte Verkabelung ist ein standardisiertes System für die gesamte Daten- und Kommunikationsverkabelung in Gebäuden. Statt für jede Anwendung separate Kabel zu verlegen – eines für Telefon, eines für Computer, eines für Drucker – nutzt ein strukturiertes System eine einheitliche Infrastruktur für alle Dienste. Das Prinzip ist simpel: Eine durchdachte, einheitliche Verkabelung bildet das Fundament, auf dem alle aktiven Netzwerkkomponenten wie [Switches, Router](https://nls-netzwerke.de/service/switching-routertechnologie/ "Switches, Router") und Access Points aufbauen. Die internationale Norm ISO/IEC 11801 sowie die europäische EN 50173 definieren dabei genau, wie eine solche Verkabelung aufgebaut sein muss. ## Die drei Ebenen der strukturierten Verkabelung Ein strukturiertes Verkabelungssystem gliedert sich in drei hierarchische Bereiche: **Primärverkabelung (Campusverkabelung):** Diese Ebene verbindet verschiedene Gebäude auf einem Firmengelände miteinander. Hier kommen fast ausschließlich Glasfaserkabel zum Einsatz, da sie große Distanzen überbrücken und hohe Bandbreiten liefern. **Sekundärverkabelung (Gebäudeverkabelung):** Sie verbindet die einzelnen Stockwerke oder Gebäudeabschnitte. The independent European leader for multi-technical services in the areas of energy and communications offers tech-savvy talents a variety of career opportunities. With a total of 28 apprenticeship occupations and eight dual study programmes, SPIE is training its own junior staff at more than 90 locations to work together with customers that make energy transition a reality and shape digital transformation. Further training is promoted: even after an apprenticeship, SPIE invests in its staff and supports the need for lifelong learning with its SPIE Academy and a variety of external training opportunities. Markus Holzke, Managing Director/CEO of SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa: "We are very proud that around 300 young talents have chosen SPIE this year. We are especially delighted that, once again, we have been able to increase the number of trainees compared to the previous year (278 in 2018) . Our new apprentices and dual students can expect an exciting time where they will learn a lot. We wish them success on their career path with SPIE" .Communal first week to become immersed in the SPIE world The first week of education began with an introduction to the SPIE world, where apprentices learn important basics, such as occupational safety. Maximilian Schrenner, Head of Recruitment and Training at SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa: "It is important to us that our apprentices and dual students, who have decided to embark on a technical or commercial career, get off to a good start with us" . Wide variety of job profiles SPIE aims to get young tech-savvy people committed to the business early on, and to give talented graduates a promising perspective at SPIE. In Germany alone, SPIE offers 28 different apprenticeship occupations and several options for a dual degree programme: from apprenticeships to plant mechanic, draughtsman, electronics technician or mechatronics technician to dual studies for a Bachelor in energy and building technology, supply engineering, technical facility management or business information technology. " We hire our experts early on, train them to meet the specific needs of our business and continue to qualify them after their training. As a multi-technical service provider, we offer an enormous variety of apprenticeship occupations and job profiles for launching a career – so anyone with a passion for technology can enjoy it to the fullest" , according to Maximilian Schrenner. Investment in training infrastructure Along with promoting young talents, SPIE is continually expanding its infrastructure for education. At the SPIE site Ergolding, near Landshut, a new training workshop for electrical and mechanical vocational training was set up for about half a million euros. "Our education is constantly evolving. In 2016, we had 20 apprentices - since September 2019, we have been educating 71 young people in six different occupations with five trainers at the Ergolding site ," says Markus Kopp, member of the South-East Regional Management of the City Networks & Grids Operational Division. SPIE's site at Ergolding was recently awarded the title of "TOP Company Lower Bavaria 2019". According to the governor of Lower Bavaria, SPIE embodies values that are important for finding, qualifying and retaining skilled workers. A lifelong training at the SPIE Academy "The continuous training of our colleagues is just as important as a good education. New solutions and technologies require long-term learning from our part. evidence.excerpt: [**Share price** **€46.56** +0.13%](/en/investors/share-price) * + [FR](https://www.spie.com/fr/journalistes/actualites/prochaine-etape-de-la-strategie-de-croissance-spie-deutschland-zentraleuropa-devient-spie-germany-switzerland-austria) ![](/sites/www.spie.com/files/styles/eco_480x338/public/2024-10/intra-banner-spie-gsa-.jpg?h=c9a3a702&itok=OiFfGdw2) * [Group](/en/group) [Press release](/en/press-release) # The next step in the growth strategy: SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa is renamed as SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria Published on 01 October 2024 **Ratingen, 1 October 2024** – *SPIE, the independent European leader in multi-technical services in the areas of energy and communications, is reorganising its operating structure and announcing the renaming of SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa as SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria.* The SPIE Group is adapting its operating structure to the company’s strong growth. Tier 1 units SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa and SPIE Switzerland will become SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria and SPIE Central Europe. SPIE Central Europe serves the markets in Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary. SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria is driving business and growth in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. **Germany has the potential to become SPIE’s largest market** “*The importance of SPIE in Germany has grown steadily within the SPIE Group over the past eleven years measured in terms of its revenue and profit contribution and employee headcount. Going forward, we see plenty of potential for further growth in the German market and we are adapting our structures to facilitate it*,” explained Gauthier Louette, Chairman & CEO of the SPIE Group. SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa’s growth strategy was launched in 2013. “*In just eleven years, Markus Holzke and his management team have developed SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa very successfully and have grown the business significantly. After three platform acquisitions and 30 bolt-on acquisitions, SPIE has evolved into the leading multi-technical service provider in Germany, Austria, Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary, and its workforce has expanded from 300 to almost 23,000 employees. That’s a fantastic achievement. I am fully confident that the management team will continue to follow this roadmap to success and develop Germany into SPIE’s biggest market*,” commented Gauthier Louette. **The company will be renamed on 1 October 2024** On 1 October 2024, SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa GmbH will be renamed as SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria GmbH. This company will be the lead company for all subsidiaries operating in Germany, Switzerland and Austria, including entities with representative offices for customers in other countries according to the “follow the customer” principle. **SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria remains on a growth trajectory** “*Our new organisational structure reflects SPIE’s comprehensive technical expertise in Germany, Switzerland, Austria and beyond. Together, we are around 20,000 team members working with our customers to establish a climate-friendly and digital future. I am very much looking forward to growing and expanding our business with the support of the entire SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria management team, and to extending the range and depth of our services*,” added Markus Holzke, Managing Director/CEO of SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria. The SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria management structure consists of eight business units organised by market and country, as well as the headquarters: * **Operational Division Efficient Facilities (EF), managed by Rainer Hollang:**Around 4,300 employees provide technical facility management, energy efficiency solutions and renewable energies (own power generation, CO2-free heat generation and cooling systems) for our customers’ buildings and sites. * **Operational Division CityNetworks & Grids (CNG), managed by Peter Pfannenstiel:**Around 5,400 team members deploy

evidence.excerpt: SPIE, sharing a vision for the future Manuel Schramm, Technician, SPIE Deutschland & ZentraleuropaInspiration 2022 Integrated Annual Report Please consider the environment before printing this document. part 01 2022 in review 12 2022 news in our 4 markets 26 Engaging with our stakeholders 18 Value-creation model 20 Our financial performance 22 Our non-financial performance introduction 04 Message from Gauthier Louette 06 SPIE’s governance in action 28 Identifying trends 30 A solid model to support trends 32 Twin transitions 34 Acquisitions 36 SPIE & Worksphere 38 CSR strategy 40 Finance and sustainable business 42 Risk management part 02 At the heart of a changing world part 03 On the road to a responsible future 46 Exploring new energy horizons 52 Driving responsible digital innovation 58 Embodying responsibility and inclusiveness for regions 64 Non-financial indicators 66 Contacts and acknowledgements Download the mobile apps @SPIE and stay tuned to SPIE news (Google Play store) Download the mobile apps @SPIE and stay tuned to SPIE news (App store) Read our report on your smartphone CONTENTS SPIE, part of the solution An accessible version of the SPIE 2022 integrated report is available at rai2022.spie.com SPIE, sharing a vision for the future After the first large-scale initiatives for the green economy in 2021, companies and public authorities took their efforts even further in 2022. Soaring demand for solutions to reduce consumption in response to increasing energy costs and active work to decarbonise operations once again enabled the SPIE Group to post excellent results this year, with organic growth of 6.9%. More than ever, SPIE is part of the solution, offering high value-added services to drive the energy transition and responsible digital transformation. Whether installing charging stations for electric vehicles, connecting new wind farms to the grid or rolling out smart maintenance tools to reduce buildings’ carbon footprints, the Group and its employees have a positive and visible impact on the environment day after day. At the same time, SPIE is leveraging its solutions to meet the commitments contained in its 2025 CSR roadmap. Our integrated report showcases a selection of our achievements for the year, underpinned by practical solutions and a determination to lead by example. We hope you enjoy reading it. 3 EDITORIAL Introduction Our fundamentals are strong, as demonstrated by our resilience during the health crisis. And we kept our strategic bearings by expanding in key energy transition markets, such as energy efficiency, industry decarbonisation, development of low-carbon energies and electric mobility solutions. The current environment does call for constant vigilance and agility. But at the same time, we are seeing unprecedented opportunities as the energy transition accelerates in response to rising energy prices and the worsening impacts of climate change. In 2022, our revenue rose in all the countries where we were operating, to total €8.1 billion, up +16.1% vs. 2021. More importantly, despite inflation, we grew our margin to 6.3%. “Our positioning working towards a low-carbon economy ensures we have bright development prospects. ” Message from Gauth ier Louette, Chairman & CEO of SPIE S PIE posted very strong results despite a turbulent geopolitical, economic and social environment. How do you explain this performance? This year SPIE acquired Worksphere in the Netherlands and sold its UK operations. What is the Group’s competitive profile after these two transactions? In the highly fragmented UK market, our business was too limited to open any real opportunities. We believed that SPIE UK would develop better with a new shareholder, so we sold all our activities in the country. We can now focus our business development on continental Europe, with a particular focus on central Europe and northern Europe – two strategic markets. findings.statement: Entity is SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria, formerly SPIE Deutschland & Zentraleuropa, with German presence and headquarters in Ratingen/Düsseldorf area, part of SPIE Group.
notes: Official and group sources confirm renaming in October 2024.

findings.statement: Candidate operates in Germany with about 20,000 employees and over 250 locations in Germany, Austria and Switzerland according to supplied evidence.
notes: Official website and group profile confirm extensive German and regional presence.

findings.statement: Company is active in information and communications technology services, including installation, upgrade, management and sourcing of voice, data and image communication systems.
notes: SPIE services descriptions and network services site support active networking involvement.

findings.statement: Company performs installation of network infrastructure, including broadband/FTTH, radio networks, charging stations and building communication systems.
notes: WirliebenKabel and official materials show planning, construction, installation and maintenance services.
Non-standard finding kind "installer-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: Company supplies system integration services for plan, build and operate phases of network solutions for enterprise and carrier customers.
notes: SPIE Network Services explicitly describes a System Integrator model and turnkey project services.
Non-standard finding kind "si-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: Company provides value-added technology services including vendor selection, procurement of hardware and software, design and consulting for network solutions.
notes: Sourcing solutions include vendor selection, procurement, pilot/PoC, design and consulting services.
Non-standard finding kind "var-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: No evidence shows the entity itself supplying downstream resellers, dealers, system houses or other channel partners.
notes: Evidence describes end-customer enterprise/carrier services, not distribution to channel partners.
Non-standard finding kind "distributor-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: Group-level evidence consistently indicates about 20,000 employees in Germany, Austria and Switzerland; some third-party legal entity profiles show a much smaller single-entity employee count.
notes: Tracxn cites 332 employees for a single legal entity as of 2021, while official/group sources refer to roughly 20,000 across the operating region.

findings.statement: SPIE serves enterprise, carrier, government and industrial customers through planning, design, building, operating and maintaining energy and communication infrastructure.
notes: Customer references and official service descriptions support end-customer commercial actions.

reasons: Resolved entity to SPIE Germany Switzerland Austria based on 2024 official renaming and current website evidence.
Installer role is directly supported by broadband, cabling, charging-station and network infrastructure installation services.
SI role is supported by explicit system-integrator engagement model and plan/build/operate descriptions.
VAR role is supported by vendor selection, procurement and value-added technology services.
Primary role is Hybrid because installer, SI and VAR families are materially co-primary, while distributor behavior is not demonstrated.

evidence.title: Wi-Fi 7 erklärt: Vorteile & Einsatz mit Glasfaser
evidence.excerpt: [News | DNSNET Internet Service GmbH](https://www.dns-net.de/news) # [Wi-Fi 7 erklärt: Vorteile, MLO & Glasfaser | DNS:NET](https://www.dns-net.de/news/wi-fi-7-vorteile-glasfaser) Geschrieben von [Iseewanga Buch](https://www.dns-net.de/news/author/iseewanga-buch) | Sep 24, 2025 12:33:02 PM ## Was ist Wi-Fi 7 und welche Vorteile bringt es? Wi-Fi 7 ist die neueste WLAN-Technologie, die für deutlich höhere Geschwindigkeiten, stabilere Verbindungen und geringere Latenzen im Heimnetz sorgt. Der größte Vorteil: Wi-Fi 7 kann mehrere Frequenzbänder gleichzeitig nutzen und verteilt die verfügbare Bandbreite effizient auf viele Geräte. Dadurch bleiben Verbindungen auch bei hoher Auslastung zuverlässig und schnell. In Kombination mit einem Glasfaseranschluss entfaltet Wi-Fi 7 sein volles Potenzial und verhindert, dass das WLAN zum Engpass wird – für reibungsloses Streaming, Gaming und Arbeiten im Homeoffice. ### Der neueste WLAN-Standard Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) ist der neue WLAN-Standard, der seit Juli 2025 finalisiert und schon heute in ersten Routern und Endgeräten verfügbar ist. Mit Multi-Link-Operation (MLO), 320-MHz-Kanälen und 4K-QAM bietet Wi-Fi 7 deutlich mehr Geschwindigkeit, Stabilität und geringere Latenzen als seine Vorgänger. Für Streaming, Gaming, Homeoffice und Smart-Home ist das ein echter Technologiesprung. In Kombination mit DNS:NET-Glasfaser entfaltet Wi-Fi 7 sein volles Potenzial. ### Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) im Detail Wi-Fi 7, auch bekannt als IEEE 802.11be, ist der neueste internationale WLAN-Standard. Am 22. Juli 2025 wurde er final verabschiedet und die [Wi-Fi Alliance](https://www.wi-fi.org/) bietet seit Anfang 2024 ein offizielles Zertifizierungsprogramm an. Gegenüber Wi-Fi 6 und 6E bringt Wi-Fi 7 wesentliche Verbesserungen: * [**Multi-Link Operation (MLO):**](https://www.dns-net.de/glossar/mlo) gleichzeitige Nutzung mehrerer Frequenzbänder (2,4/5/6 GHz) → mehr Stabilität, geringere Latenzen. * Breitere Kanäle bis [320 MHz](https://www.dns-net.de/news/320-mhz-kanal-wifi7): Verdopplung der Bandbreite ggü. Wi-Fi 6. * [4K-QAM-Modulation](https://www.dns-net.de/glossar/4k-qam)**:** rund 20 % mehr Spitzenleistung. * Verbesserte [MU-MIMO](https://www.dns-net.de/glossar/mu-mimo) und [OFDMA](https://www.dns-net.de/glossar/ofdma) für effizientere Netzwerknutzung. Kurz gesagt: Wi-Fi 7 ist das WLAN der nächsten Generation – entwickelt für datenintensive Anwendungen wie 4K/8K-Streaming, Cloud-Gaming oder Homeoffice. Mit DNS:NET-Glasfaser wird die volle Leistung nutzbar – ohne Flaschenhals im Netz. > [**Passende Glasfaser-Tarife mit Wi-Fi-7-Router ansehen**](https://www.dns-net.de/glasfaser/tarife) ### Die wichtigsten Neuerungen von Wi-Fi 7 Wi-Fi 7 bringt eine Reihe technischer Innovationen, die das Heimnetz deutlich leistungsfähiger machen. Hier die zentralen Features, klar erklärt: #### Multi-Link Operation (MLO) Herzstück von Wi-Fi 7: Router und Endgeräte können mehrere Frequenzbänder (2,4/5/6 GHz) gleichzeitig nutzen. * Ergebnis: geringere Latenzen, stabilere Verbindungen, weniger Ausfälle bei Störungen. * Besonders wichtig für Gaming, VR und Videokonferenzen. #### 320-MHz-Kanäle * Verdopplung der Kanalbreite im Vergleich zu Wi-Fi 6 (160 MHz → 320 MHz). * Mehr Bandbreite = höhere Spitzendurchsätze von über 40 Gbit/s im Labor. * In der Praxis: spürbare Performance-Steigerung bei datenintensiven Anwendungen wie 8K-Streaming. #### 4K-QAM-Modulation * Höhere Signalverdichtung: rund 20 % mehr Durchsatz als Wi-Fi 6 (1024-QAM). * Vorteil: effizientere Nutzung des Funkspektrums. * Hinweis: Erfordert stabile Signalqualität – daher besonders im Glasfaserumfeld sinnvoll. #### Verbesserte Effizienz-Features * Optimierungen bei MU-MIMO (mehr gleichzeitige Verbindungen) und OFDMA (effiziente Aufteilung der Kanäle). * **[Puncturing](https://www.dns-net.de/glossar/channel-puncturing)/Multi-RU**: bessere Nutzung von Kanälen auch bei Störungen. * Ergebnis: mehr Kapazität für Smarthomes mit vielen Geräten. ### Wi-Fi 7 in Deutschland Während in d

Dann prüfe jetzt die passende Lösung für Deinen Glasfaseranschluss.* [Passenden Router finden](https://www.dns-net.de/router) In diesem FAQ erfährst du: * welcher Router zu einem Glasfaseranschluss von DNS:NET passt * wann sich Wi-Fi 7, Mesh-WLAN oder ein einfacher Router lohnt * welche Sicherheitsfunktionen 2026 Pflicht sind * welche Lösungen wir für Familien, Mieter:innen, Eigentümer:innen, Gamer:innen und Senior:innen empfehlen ``` ``` ### Was ist 2026 bei der Routerwahl besonders wichtig? 2026 müssen Router vorrangig eines sein: zukunftssicher und leistungsstark. Das heißt: * Unterstützung für Wi-Fi 6, 6E oder Wi-Fi 7. Inzwischen Standard für stabile, schnelle Verbindungen. * Multi-Gigabit-Anschlüsse (mindestens 1 Gbps, besser 2,5 Gbps oder SFP+) passend zu heutigen Glasfaseranschlüssen. * Leistungsfähiges Mesh-WLAN für lückenlose Abdeckung. * Moderne Sicherheitsfunktionen wie WPA3, automatische Updates und eine integrierte Firewall. * Eine einfache, intuitive Bedienung per App oder über die Weboberfläche für alle Haushaltsmitglieder. ### Brauche ich einen speziellen Router für Glasfaser? Ja. Ein moderner Glasfaseranschluss erfordert weiterhin einen Router mit WAN-Port (mindestens 1 Gbps, besser 2,5 Gbps) oder SFP+-Slot. Viele aktuelle Modelle ab 2025 und 2026 unterstützen Multi-Gigabit zuverlässig. DNS:NET stellt dir eine Kompatibilitätsliste bereit und berät dich persönlich, damit alles reibungslos funktioniert. ### Worauf sollte ich bei einem Wi‑Fi‑7‑Router achten? Ein [moderner Wi-Fi-7-Router](/router) entscheidet 2026 spürbar darüber, ob dein Glasfaseranschluss seine volle Leistung entfalten kann. Achte besonders auf: * **Multi-Link Operation (MLO)**: parallele Nutzung mehrerer Bänder für höhere Stabilität und geringere Latenz. * **Tri-Band-Unterstützung:** optimale Lastverteilung für Streaming, Gaming und Smart Home. * **2,5-G- und 10-G-Ports:** wichtig für Multi-Gigabit-Glasfaseranschlüsse. * **Mesh-Funktionalität:** für größere Wohnungen, Altbauten und Häuser in Berlin und Brandenburg. * **Security:** WPA3 als Standard, regelmäßige Updates und ein klarer Update-Pfad hin zu WPA4. * **Glasfaseroptimierung**: Router sollten Bandbreiten von 500 Mbit/s bis 10 Gbit/s vollständig durchleiten. ### Welcher WLAN-Standard ist sinnvoll: Wi-Fi 6, 6E oder 7? Wi-Fi 6 ist weiterhin ein solider Standard für viele Haushalte. Wi‑Fi 6E nutzt zusätzlich das störungsarme 6‑GHz-Band und ist ideal in dicht bebauten Stadtlagen mit vielen Nachbar-WLANs. evidence.title: DNS:NET setzt neue Maßstäbe im Glasfasermarkt: 10-GBit-Technologie ab Oktober
evidence.excerpt: [News | DNSNET Internet Service GmbH](https://www.dns-net.de/news) # [DNS:NET bringt 10 Gbit/s-Technologie & Wi-Fi 7 nach Deutschland](https://www.dns-net.de/news/10-gbit-wifi7-xgs-pon-glasfaser-technologie-dnsnet) Geschrieben von [Claudia Burkhardt](https://www.dns-net.de/news/author/claudia-burkhardt) | Oct 16, 2025, 12:45:49 PM Auf der Basis von XGS-PON und der neuen Wi-Fi 7 Tri-Band-Lösung gibt es Glasfaserprodukte der Spitzenklasse **[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)** Berlin, 16. Oktober 2025 – Nachdem auf dem [NetworkX-Event](https://networkxevent.com/) in Paris von der DNS:NET der Einsatz der [neuen Wi-Fi-7-Tri-Band-Lösung](https://www.dns-net.de/news/zte-dnsnet-wifi7-xgspon-tri-band-loesung-deutschland) demonstriert wurde, stellt die DNS:NET ihr neues Produktportfolio für die Breitbandversorgung in Deutschland vor. Ab sofort erhalten Neukunden und Bestandskunden standardmäßig im neuen Portfolio den neuen Wi-Fi-7-Tri-Band-Router. #### ****DNS:NET führt mit der neuen 10-GBit/s-Technologie einen High-End-Standard für Privatkunden ein**** Jeder Privatkunde kann ab sofort neben dem beliebten 1-GBit/s-Tarif „DERTarif“ auch einen neuen Glasfaser-Tarif mit modernster 10-GBit/s-Technologie buchen. In Kombination mit dem neuen Wi-Fi-7-Tri-Band-Router bietet DNS:NET damit eine Highspeed-Lösung der nächsten Generation. Mit DNS:NET-Glasfaser kommt so die besonders stabile 10-GBit/s-Technologie direkt bis ins Zuhause. DNS:NET-Kunden erhalten damit auch die neuesten Router auf Basis von Wi-Fi 7. Der neue DNS:NET Premium-Router mit Wi-Fi 7 Tri-Band ist ab sofort bei allen Glasfasertarifen inklusive – vorkonfiguriert und sofort einsatzbereit. DNS:NET ist somit einer der ersten Anbieter in Deutschland, die Wi-Fi-7-Router mit Tri-Band für Glasfaseranschlüsse mit 10-GBit/s-Technologie einsetzen. > „Mit 10 GBit/s Glasfaser – dem sogenannten XGS-PON und Wi-Fi 7 bringen wir die Zukunft direkt ins Wohnzimmer. Unsere Mission bleibt: Menschen mit Lichtgeschwindigkeit begeistern – regional, unabhängig und auf dem modernsten Stand der Technik.“, so Kim Juchem, CCO der DNS:NET. ****Die Fakten im Überblick:**** * **10 GBit/s-Technologie** (Line-Rate, XGS-PON) bzw. typisch 8–8,5 GBit/s netto symmetrisch an DNS:NET-Glasfaseradressen * **Router inklusive**in allen Tarifen – keine Zusatzkosten, keine Konfigurationshürden * **High-End-Internet** wird massenmarktfähig; jeder kann sich 10-GBit/s-Technologie leisten (19,99 € für die ersten 12 Monate). Der neue symmetrische Privatkundentarif kostet 99 € im Monat und beinhaltet den Wi-Fi-7-Router bereits. In den ersten zwölf Monaten bietet DNSNET den Tarif für nur 19,99 € an, sodass alle Kunden das High-Speed-Wunder testen können. * Ausbau- und Versorgungsgebiete erhalten automatisch das **volle Potenzial auf Basis von XGS-PON**.**[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)****[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)****[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)****[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)** **[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)** #### ****Technik auf einen Blick**** **[](https://www.dns-net.de/news/glasfaserausbau-falkensee)** ****Wi-Fi 7** bringt eine Reihe technischer Innovationen für mehr Leistungsfähigkeit:** * **Multi-Link Operation (MLO):** Die Router und Endgeräte können mehrere Frequenzbänder (2,4/5/6 GHz) gleichzeitig nutzen. Somit gibt es geringere Latenzen, stabilere Verbindungen und damit weniger Ausfälle bei Störungen. * **320-MHz-Kanäle** führen zur Verdopplung der Kanalbreite im Vergleich zu Wi-Fi 6 (160 MHz→MHz → 320 MHz). Im Ergebnis gibt es bis zu 40 Gbit/s theoretische Spitzendurchsätze im Labor – deutlich mehr Bandbreite und stabilere Verbindungen. Dadurch gibt es eine spürbare Performance-Steigerung bei datenintensiven Anwendungen (u.a. 8K-Streaming, VR, Videokonferenz etc.). * **4K-QAM-Modulation:** Das bedeutet – es gibt eine höhere Signalverdichtung. Rund zwan

[Proceed to site](# "3i Infrastructure") [Terms and conditions](/about-us/ "About us") 3i-infrastructure Logo * [Home](/) * [Newsroom](/newsroom/) * [Press releases](/newsroom/press-releases/) * [3i Infrastructure plc agrees to acquire DNS:NET](/newsroom/press-releases/2021/3i-infrastructure-plc-agrees-to-acquire-dnsnet/) # Newsroom # 3i Infrastructure plc agrees to acquire DNS:NET ![Dns Net Wulkau 2016 1241](/media/2oukap3k/dns_net_wulkau_2016_1241.jpg?width=856&height=535&v=1db4bdc1dd5c9c0) **3i Infrastructure plc (“3i Infrastructure”) has agreed to invest c.€182m to acquire a 60% stake in DNS:NET and to provide additional funding for the future growth of the business. DNS:NET is a leading independent telecommunications provider in Germany.** 3i Infrastructure is buying its stake from Deutsche Beteiligungs AG (“DBAG”), DBAG ECF, a private equity fund managed by DBAG, and Founder and CEO Alexander Lucke, with the latter reinvesting alongside 3i Infrastructure to retain a 40% stake. Completion is expected to take place in June 2021. Established in 1998, DNS:NET owns the largest independent fibre-to-the-cabinet network in the Berlin area, as well as three data centres. The company differentiates itself through a superior network, local brand recognition and attractive pricing of high bandwidth products, which drives high customer satisfaction. In recent years, DNS:NET has commenced a fibre-to-the-home (“FTTH”) rollout which it now plans to accelerate with 3i Infrastructure’s backing. Fibre is superior to other broadband access technologies because it provides reliable low latency, high bandwidth and distance-independent connectivity for both download and upload. Demand for FTTH connectivity is forecast to grow rapidly, as consumers normalise data intensive activities such as cloud-based remote working, high definition streaming and online gaming, and increasingly view high speed broadband as an essential service. Germany lags behind most European countries in its FTTH deployment, with only 14% coverage today compared to the European average of 33%. The market is projected to grow at 30% p.a. to meet the German government’s objective of every one of its 43 million households having access to gigabit speed broadband by 2025. Richard Laing, Chair of 3i Infrastructure, commented: “DNS:NET is an asset-intensive business delivering an essential service in a sector with strong underlying demand trends. It is a high growth asset which will further diversify our portfolio, giving 3i Infrastructure sizeable exposure to the German infrastructure market for the first time.” Phil White, Managing Partner and Head of Infrastructure, 3i Investments plc, Investment Manager of 3i Infrastructure, added: “For businesses and consumers alike, fibre connectivity is increasingly a necessity as data and computing power moves to the cloud. Alexander has built a highly successful business over more than 20 years and we look forward to partnering with him and his management team as DNS:NET rolls out its fibre-to-the-home offering in Berlin and the surrounding area.” Peter Wirtz, co-Managing Director 3i Germany, commented: “Alexander is an impressive entrepreneur, who has built a highly regarded business, and we are delighted to be backing him and his management team. We are also pleased to be expanding into the German infrastructure market which we think offers attractive opportunities.”

findings.statement: The legal entity is DNS:NET Internet Service GmbH, also operating as DNS:NET.
notes: Official website, North Data trade register profile, LinkedIn, and 3i Infrastructure press release all use the same legal name.

findings.statement: The company-owned official domain is dns-net.de, reached at https://www.dns-net.de/.
notes: The official company pages and navigation are on www.dns-net.de. LinkedIn also lists https://www.dns-net.de/ as the website.
Non-standard finding kind "official-website" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company is headquartered in Berlin, Germany and operates primarily in Berlin, Brandenburg, and Saxony-Anhalt.
notes: Official website, trade register, LinkedIn, and independent profiles consistently place the company in Berlin with operations in Berlin, Brandenburg, and Saxony-Anhalt.

findings.statement: DNS:NET is active in telecommunications networking and operates its own fiber network infrastructure.
notes: Official company page, 3i Infrastructure press release, wlw profile, Genexis case study, and presseportal release describe owned fiber networks, data centers, and broadband network operations.

findings.statement: DNS:NET operates as an Internet Service Provider, delivering internet, telephony, and TV services over its own fiber and VDSL network infrastructure.
notes: Multiple independent sources, including Genexis, IT-in-Germany, Trustpilot, and wlw, classify DNS:NET as a telecommunications provider or ISP. 3i Infrastructure describes it as an independent telecommunications provider owning fiber networks and data centers.
Non-standard finding kind "business-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: The submitted Distributor role is not supported by any evidence showing the company supplying products to downstream resellers, dealers, system houses, or channel partners.
notes: The supplied evidence shows a network operator and connectivity service provider. No source mentions distribution of third-party products to channel partners, resellers, or dealers. Open Access agreements and wholesale bitstream arrangements are carrier/network relationships, not product distribution.
Non-standard finding kind "business-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: DNS:NET reports approximately 250 employees, with some directory estimates ranging from 166 to nearly 400.
notes: Official company page and LinkedIn state about 250 employees. GetLatka estimates 166, PitchBook reports 250, and wlw states nearly 400. Evidence is materially positive for company size; the company is not a small long-tail micro-business.

findings.statement: The company offers fiber broadband, VDSL, IPTV, telephony, and business IP-based services, and provides routers as part of its service portfolio.
notes: Official website and press releases describe 10 Gbit/s fiber products, Wi-Fi 7 routers included with tariffs, IPTV, telephony, SIP trunking, VoIP, VPN, and data-center services.

findings.statement: DNS:NET uses Wi-Fi 7 router technology and works with suppliers such as ZTE and Genexis for customer-premises equipment.
notes: Press releases mention a ZTE/DNS:NET Wi-Fi 7 XGS-PON tri-band solution. Genexis lists DNS:NET as a customer case. These relationships are customer-equipment supplier relationships, not distribution or resale of third-party products.

findings.statement: DNS:NET provides collective wholesale bitstream access and Open Access cooperation to other network operators.
notes: Presseportal release reports that vitroconnect purchases FTTC bitstream from DNS:NET and that DNS:NET participates in an Open Access Allianz. These are carrier-to-carrier wholesale arrangements, not distributor sales to channel partners.

reasons: Official and independent evidence consistently identifies DNS:NET as an independent telecommunications provider and ISP operating its own fiber and VDSL networks.
The submitted Distributor role lacks evidence of supplying downstream resellers, dealers, or channel partners.
The original distribution search lane was treated only as diagnostic provenance and not used as a primary-role input.
The company's defining business action is providing connectivity services on owned network infrastructure, matching the ISP role.
warnings: Submitted Distributor role was not supported by any supplied evidence.
Independent directory estimates for employee count vary and should be treated with caution.

findings.statement: The company operates as ESA GmbH German Protect, with German Protect as a trading brand.
