LinkedIn company page confirms 'ESA GmbH German Protect'.

findings.statement: The legal entity is German Protect Secura GmbH, while the operating brand is ESA GmbH German Protect.
notes: North Data records 'German Protect Secura GmbH' at Speyer.
The official website and LinkedIn use 'ESA GmbH German Protect'. The exact legal entity resolution remains partly ambiguous.
Non-standard finding kind "company-name" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company is located in Speyer, Rheinland-Pfalz, Germany.
notes: LinkedIn lists address Nachtweide 2, Speyer, Rheinland-Pfalz 67346, DE.
North Data also shows Germany.

findings.statement: The company sells networking products, including routers, switches and access points, online.
notes: Official website product pages list Ubiquiti, LANCOM, Dahua and other networking products.
Titles include 'Fachhändler' and online shop language, indicating direct online sale.

findings.statement: The company operates a direct-to-customer online shop selling security and networking technology.
notes: Cart and account icons and product catalogue indicate online sales.
More than 40,000 to 50,000 products referenced for the online shop.
Non-standard finding kind "role-e-tailer" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company presents itself as a specialist dealer or Fachhändler for security and network products.
notes: Official site titles such as 'vom Fachhändler' support a dealer positioning.
Non-standard finding kind "role-dealer" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company resells third-party products such as Ubiquiti, LANCOM, Dahua and Ajax.
notes: The shop carries multiple third-party brands.
Brand partnerships include Ajax Systems, Eneo, Bosch, Seetec and Milestone.
Non-standard finding kind "role-reseller" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company acts as a certified specialist installer (Fach-Errichter) for security technology.
notes: Official B2B page states 'zertifizierten Fach-Errichter' and refers to Montage.
LinkedIn states services include planning, project engineering, installation and alarm integration.
Non-standard finding kind "role-installer" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company provides project planning, project engineering and integrated security services from a single source.
notes: The B2B page describes Projektierung, Montage, Monitoring, Schulungen, Wartungsservice and Alarmaufschaltung aus einer Hand.
LinkedIn describes holistic project support for security projects.
The SI positioning is service-led rather than purely product-led; therefore confidence is moderate.
Non-standard finding kind "role-si" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company supplies downstream resellers, dealers or channel partners.
notes: North Data describes the company object as 'distribution of non-authorisational security components in the commercial and private sector', which may refer to selling rather than true channel distribution.
The SourceSecurity directory listing is a directory page and does not provide specific evidence that German Protect itself distributes to other resellers.
No supplied evidence shows supply to downstream channel partners.
Non-standard finding kind "role-distributor" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The company offers video surveillance, networking, access points, routers and mobile surveillance towers.
notes: Products include Ubiquiti switches, access points and routers, LANCOM devices, Dahua cameras and video transmission products.
A blog article describes mobile video surveillance towers.
Non-standard finding kind "product-families" was normalized to product-family.

findings.statement: The company reports partnerships with Ajax Systems, Eneo, Bosch, Seetec and Milestone.
notes: A blog article states 'unserem Partner Ajax Systems, Eneo System Integrator, Bosch Partner, Seetec Professional, Milestone'.
Non-standard finding kind "brand-relationships" was normalized to brand-relationship.

findings.statement: LinkedIn lists the company as having 11-50 employees and two associated LinkedIn members.
notes: This is a self-reported LinkedIn size band, not verified by registry or financial documents.

findings.statement: The company provides B2B project support including planning, installation, monitoring, training, maintenance and alarm integration.
notes: The B2B page lists these services for public institutions and commercial customers.
Non-standard finding kind "business-actions" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: The evidence does not demonstrate a distributor cooperation path because no downstream channel supply is shown.
notes: North Data wording 'distribution ... in the commercial and private sector' is insufficient to prove supply to other resellers.
SourceSecurity entries are directory listings and do not provide specific German Protect activities.

reasons: The submitted company name 'GermanProtect' should be corrected to the combined brand/legal identity ESA GmbH German Protect as shown on official and LinkedIn sources.
The official online shop and pages describing the company as a certified Fach-Errichter support simultaneous direct retail/E-tail and installation/system-integration roles.
Both E-tailer/Dealer and Installer/SI role families are materially present, so Hybrid is the appropriate primary role.
No supplied evidence proves that German Protect itself supplies downstream resellers or channel partners, so Distributor is not supported.
The SourceSecurity and SecurityInformed directory pages provide no specific evidence about this candidate's activities and therefore cannot support a Distributor role.
warnings: The SourceSecurity and SecurityInformed directory URLs are generic directory pages and do not specifically mention German Protect.

The German name 'German Protect Secura GmbH' from North Data may refer to the legal entity, while the trade identity ESA GmbH German Protect is used on the website; legal entity resolution is not fully certain.
Directory-based evidence should not be treated as proof of a Distributor role for this candidate.
Roles without a supported atomic role finding were removed.
Deterministic role hints were not auto-added: Distributor, E-tailer, SI, Reseller.

'$& '##(%# !&'(& "'$ $'(%( &"'$'('%#$ '(% ''%#( %(!% "$#"!%& &%'%( $( "&((('&&(!"%#& Mit dem Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC lassen sich große WLAN-Netzwerke zentral managen Die Anwendungen von WLAN in der Automati-sierung werden immer vielfältiger. Der Standard IEEE 802.1 1n ermöglicht mit der OpenBAT Familie Datenraten von bis zu 450 Mbit/s und erhöht zugleich die Reichweite und die Sta-bilität der Funkübertragung. Ein zentrales Management gewährleistet auch erweiterte Sicherheitsfunktionen und biete einen zentra-len Überblick auf das Netzwerk. Speziell hierfür wurde der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC entwickelt. Bereits installierte Hirschmann™ Access Points der BAT-Familie müssen nicht durch Controller-taugliche Geräte ersetzt werden – diese Access Points können sowohl mit als auch ohne Controller betrieben werden. So lässt sich ein Funknetzwerk Schritt für Schritt aufbauen und sobald erforderlich um Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC ergänzen. Vom Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC gibt es sechs Varianten: • Hirschmann BAT-Controller WLC25, 50, 100, 200, 500 und 1000: Mit diesen Lösungen lassen sich zwischen 25 und 1000 Access Points verwalten. Produktmerkmale • Automatische Konfiguration und zentrales Management sämtlicher Access Points des Funknetzwerks • Kompatibel zu allen Hirschmann™ Access Points der BAT-Familie • Voller Durchsatz der Nutzdaten gemäß IEEE 802.1 1n pro Access Point • Integrierter IP-Router mit Firewall und VPN-Unterstützung • Nutzer-Authentifizierung gemäß IEEE 802.1x, RADIUS und LEPS • Fast Roaming über mehrere Sub-Netzwerke hinweg • Automatisches Frequenzmanagement im 2,4- und 5-GHz-Band • Hohe Verfügbarkeit durch Redundanz- und Backup-Mechanismen • Verbindung mehrerer WLAN-Netzwerke mittels VPN-Gateway-Funktion • 19"-Gerät für den Einsatz im Kontrollraum 2 Der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC Bereits beim Aufbau des Netzwerks findet der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC alle darin vor -handenen Access Points. Anschließend überprüft der Controller, ob die Access Points die richtige Firmware haben und konfiguriert sie entsprechend der jeweiligen Applikation. So wird dem Admi-nistrator schon beim Aufbau des Netzwerks viel Arbeit abgenommen. Während des Betriebs stellt der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC alle erforderlichen Netzwerkinformationen zur Verfügung. Sollte ein Access Point ausfallen, erkennt der Controller das Austauschgerät sofort und bindet es automatisch in das Netzwerk ein. Die Management-Software muss also nicht mehr bei jedem Access Point die Daten einzeln abfragen. Dadurch wird die Netzlast reduziert und die Informationen stehen schneller zur Verfügung. Mit dem Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC können zudem weitere Funktionen realisiert werden, die ohne einen vollständigen Überblick über das WLAN-Netzwerk nicht möglich wären. Das Netz-werk lässt sich beispielsweise so einrichten, dass die Kanalverteilung zu möglichst wenigen Über-lappungen und Störungen zwischen den einzelnen Access Points führt. Außerdem kann der WLAN-Controller als zentrale Firewall und Security-Instanz zwischen dem kabelgebundenen und dem drahtlosen Teil des Netzwerks fungieren. Der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC lässt sich auch als VPN-Gateway einsetzen, um mehrere WLAN-Netzwerke auch über große Distanzen miteinander zu verbinden. Dies ist insbesondere für Unternehmen mit mehreren Standorten von Vorteil. Der Hirschmann™ BAT-Controller WLC sorgt für eine hohe Verfügbarkeit des Funknetzwerks. 3 Port-Typ und Anzahl Typ BAT-Controller WLC25 BAT-Controller WLC50 BAT-Controller WLC100 BAT-Controller WLC200 BAT-Controller WLC500 BAT-Controller WLC1000 Bestell-Nummer 942 034-001 942 034-002 942 034-003 942 034-004 942 034-005 942 034-006 Smart Controller Technology Der WLAN Controller unterstützt pro Funkzelle/SSID unterschiedliche Auskopplung der Nutzdaten: • Direkt

evidence.excerpt: ![Hopf bei Sonnenaufgang](/_next/image?url=%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fhopf-ueber-uns.webp&w=3840&q=75) # Wer sind wir? HOPF ist ein gewachsenes Technologie- und Vertriebsunternehmen für Automatisierungs- und Netzwerktechnik. Was 1938 als kleines Vertriebsbüro in Frankfurt am Main begann, ist heute ein Partner für Komplettlösungen mit tiefer Markterfahrung, engem Hersteller-Netzwerk und einem Team, das Technik mit Praxis verbindet. ## HOPF: Ihr Partner für Automatisierungstechnik Fortschritt seit 1938 – dafür steht HOPF. Seit dem Unternehmensstart wurde aus einem kleinen Vertriebsbüro in Frankfurt am Main einer der größten Anbieter für Komplettlösungen im Bereich **Industrial Ethernet** und **Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT)**. Und das nicht ohne Grund: Zukunftsorientierte Prozesse gehören für uns seit jeher zum Erfolg. Deshalb bieten wir individuell angepasste Lösungen an, um den speziellen Anforderungen unserer Kunden im Bereich industrieller Kommunikation und IIoT immer aufs Neue gerecht zu werden. Dabei stehen wir unseren Kunden mit Best-in-Class-Produkten und umfangreichen Dienstleistungen für den Betrieb ihrer industriellen Anwendungen zur Seite. ## Zukunftsweisende Lösungen für alle Branchen Um diesem hohen Anspruch gerecht zu werden, setzt sich unser engagiertes Team kompetent und flexibel mit jeglichen technischen Kriterien auseinander – und verfügt über ein tiefgehendes Produkt- und Marktwissen. Zudem profitieren unsere Kunden von den langjährigen, partnerschaftlichen Verbindungen, die wir zu den Herstellern pflegen. Kombiniert mit unserer breiten, branchenabgestimmten Produktpalette für Anwendungen in der Elektromechanik bietet HOPF Ihnen so einen Rundum-Service. Ob im Bereich der Automatisierung, des Maschinenbaus oder des elektronischen Gerätebaus – wir begleiten Sie gerne auf dem Weg in die digitale Automatisierung! Beste Qualität bei unseren Produkten sowie unseren Dienstleistungen – das ist unser Anspruch. Dabei stehen eine kunden- und lösungsorientierte Beratung im Vordergrund. Wir stehen Ihnen als Partner beratend bei allen Problemstellungen zur Seite. Von der Planung, über die passenden Produkte bis hin zur Umsetzung – wir schaffen Ihnen eine innovative Lösung für Ihre individuellen Wünsche. Unsere Zuverlässigkeit, Kontinuität und Expertise machen uns dabei zu einem wertvollen Partner für unsere Kunden. ### Haben Sie ein Projekt im Kopf? evidence.title: eUICC (eSIM) - The new technology for SIM-enabled routers
evidence.excerpt: ![m2m Germany](https://www.m2mgermany.de/app/themes/m2mgermany/dist/Components/BasisHeader/Assets/m2m_logo_new-7ee1fec2e5.svg) # eUICC (eSIM) - The new technology for SIM-enabled routers ## What is eUICC (eSIM)? eUICCs are often also referred to as eSIMs. eSIM refers to a solderable SIM chip. The eUICC, on the other hand, is independent of the SIM card format, and is available for both chip SIMs and plastic SIM cards. This means that older products can also be retrofitted with eUICC. This eliminates one of the biggest challenges in the installation and service of mobile routers. SIM cards that have to be installed before or during operation are no longer practical for many devices. A SIM that can be reprogrammed is the solution. The latest incarnation for the time being is the eSIM or chip SIM. This is a solderable SIM chip and there are now also smaller formats such as XS-Quad. Due to this nomenclature, there is often confusion with the eUICC, i.e. the SIM card onto which one can download various profiles, so-called subscriptions. ## What are the advantages of the new technology? The SIM card can be provided with a new provider profile over the air. This means that the SIM card no longer needs to be replaced when the operator changes - minimizing sources of error and shortening maintenance and thus also the downtimes of machines and vehicles. Another advantage of the eUICC is that the mobile operator can be changed, whether for the consumer eSIM or the M2M eSIM, and without having to change the physical SIM card. The added value of this solution is that the end customer receives the hardware and software as before and is also free to choose his mobile network operator. ## Is the eSIM the solution for M2M data communication? The SIM tariffs have been adapted to the needs of both end users and M2M applications. Changing mobile operator is now the norm - even for the use of SIM cards in the M2M sector. In the partner webinar with NetModule, we explain the background to eUICC (eSIM), highlight its development, shed light on the differences between SIM and eSIM and explain the advantages of this technology for SIM-enabled routers. ## Routers for industry and general applications The NB800 is a router with a soldered-in mobile radio modem, while the NB1800 is designed with a modular modem and can be equipped with up to two modems and two SIM cards. The eUICCs are also available in the common formats FF2 (Mini-SIM) and FF3 (Micro-SIM), so that the entire NetModule portfolio can be upgraded with eUICC. ![](https://www.m2mgermany.de/app/uploads/2022/01/5210_NB800-L-front-120x0-c-default.jpg) ### NB800 vehicle router The NB800 with E-Mark provides vehicles with a robust in-vehicle internet connection. The router is ideal for mobile connectivity in a wide range of transportation and industrial applications. The compact router provides key technologies for all applications on the Internet, but also for intranet sites and remote stations that can be connected via its powerful VPN protocol suite including OpenVPN and IPsec. The integrated modem supports MIMO LTE and ensures WWAN connectivity at up to 100 Mbps. [To m2m store](https://www.m2mgermany.de/en/shop/produkt/nb800-lsu-e-fahrzeugrouter/) ![](https://www.m2mgermany.de/app/uploads/2024/03/4580_nb1800_front-e1710250977586-120x0-c-default.jpg) ### NB1800 industrial router The NB1800-LWac-G industrial router from NetModule is a powerful router for fast Internet access. The 450 MHz radio network is to gradually become a crisis-proof radio network for precisely this target group and drive forward its digitalization. A total of 1,600 radio masts are to be erected across Germany by 2025. This is because the 450 MHz radio network is fail-safe and crisis-proof, i.e. it continues to function even in the event of power outages or other disruptions - essential, as people need a reliable supply of electricity and water even in times of crisis. ![Board](/app/themes/m2mgermany/assets/icons/m2m/color/platine.svg) ## What is the 450 MHz radio network? The 450 MHz radio network is a wireless communication system that operates on a frequency of 450 megahertz (MHz). The frequency band is considered to be very robust and allows reliable communication over long distances of several kilometers with very good penetration properties in buildings. This makes it suitable for use in remote areas, for example to monitor and read smart metering systems (e.g. electricity meters) remotely, to control systems and to communicate in the event of a crisis. Compared to other mobile communications technologies such as 5G or LTE, relatively few radio masts are needed to provide a stable infrastructure across the board. This technology therefore performs extremely well compared to other mobile technologies due to its more favorable propagation characteristics. The backbone of every wireless network is formed by the base stations and transmission masts, which are responsible for sending and receiving signals. In addition to the physical infrastructure, such a network also includes a necessary backhaul connection that links the base stations to the core network. These connections can be made via various media, including cables, microwave links or even satellites. Another key component of the network structure are the end devices, i.e. the devices used by the end users. These include radio devices (cell phones), routers, intelligent smart meters or data modules in vehicles that enable direct communication with the network. Reliability in the event of a blackout is guaranteed, among other things, by the fact that there is an emergency power supply and redundant infrastructure so that operation can be maintained for up to 72 hours. Because even at 450 MHz, nothing works without power! ## Avoid blackouts with the 450 MHz radio network Reliability in the event of a blackout is guaranteed, among other things, by the fact that there is an emergency power supply and redundant infrastructure so that operation can be maintained for up to 72 hours. LORIOT is both a software provider and a network operator. LORIOT's LoRaWAN® infrastructure is continuously growing across countries. The user-friendly software platform enables LORIOT's users to build, operate and scale a secure IoT network. Solutions from LORIOT are considered extremely powerful and secure in the market. The Swiss company counts telecom and utility companies as well as system integrators, local/city authorities, blue chip companies and multinational organizations among its customer base. LORIOT provides secure connectivity for thousands of gateways, millions of devices and critical data routing. findings.statement: The candidate is m2m Germany GmbH, a German legal entity based in Wehrheim.
notes: RocketReach confirms the GmbH legal form and Wehrheim address; the official site uses m2m Germany branding.

findings.statement: m2m Germany operates in Germany, with an address in Wehrheim, Hessen.
notes: Official site content is in German and targets German market topics such as the 450 MHz radio network; independent sources confirm German address.

findings.statement: m2m Germany participates in the IoT/wireless networking ecosystem as a supplier and partner, including LoRaWAN and M2M router technologies.
notes: Content covers IoT and M2M networking technologies, partnerships, and trade-show participation.
Non-standard finding kind "active-networking-involvement" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: m2m Germany is described as a value-added distributor and offers a multi-vendor IoT/M2M shop covering manufacturers such as Laird, Owasys, AcSiP, Fibocom, Huawei, Sparklan, NetModule, AMIT and others.
notes: Actility press release explicitly uses the phrase 'value-added distributor'; the official partner and manufacturer pages list multiple manufacturers whose products appear in m2m's shop.
Non-standard finding kind "distributor-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: m2m Germany operates a web shop and sells wireless networking products directly to customers.
notes: Although 'Reseller' and 'E-tailer' are not submitted roles, an online store selling products is directly evidenced; retained as separately supported role activity. Primary-role analysis still treats channel distribution and SI as the dominant business families in the evidence.
Non-standard finding kind "reseller-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: Actility states m2m Germany proceeds as a system integrator and LoRaWAN full-service provider.
notes: Actility press release describes SI status and LoRaWAN full-service offering; LORIOT release says m2m Germany can offer all components and software for 'sensor-to-cloud' applications.
Non-standard finding kind "system-integrator-role" was normalized to role.

findings.statement: m2m Germany supplies downstream channel partners such as system houses as part of its strategic partner network.
notes: Partner page lists system houses among partners; Actility describes m2m Germany as a value-added distributor and Premium Channel Partner, indicating a channel-facing supply role.
Non-standard finding kind "distributor-downstream-supply" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: m2m Germany maintains manufacturer/partner relationships with Actility, LORIOT, Telkom, Laird Connectivity, NetModule, Fibocom, Huawei, Silicon Labs and numerous other IoT/M2M manufacturers.
notes: Official partner page and independent press releases document multiple brand and partner relationships.
Non-standard finding kind "brand-relationships" was normalized to brand-relationship.

findings.statement: m2m Germany launched a sales partnership with Techship to act as official sales agent for embedded products in the DACH region.
notes: Official-site announcement of DACH sales agency shows active channel sales activity.

reasons: Submitted identity and distributor/VAD/SI roles are largely supported by official and independent evidence.
Official domain m2mgermany.de is directly demonstrated by multiple official-site evidence items.
Distributor and VAD roles are supported by Actility's 'value-added distributor' and 'Premium Channel Partner' language plus multi-vendor official shop.
System Integrator role is independently supported by Actility and LORIOT sources.
Primary role was set to Hybrid rather than using the original distribution search lane as proof.

evidence.excerpt: # Meet Germany's top 30 IT distributors #### Ingram, ALSO and Tech Data dominate but there's no shortage of local heroes in the German distribution market, according to our sister title Channelnomics Did you know that seven cents in every euro spent on ICT in Germany travels through just three giant IT distributors? That's one of the more surprising findings of research into the top 30 ICT distributors in Germany which has been carried out by our sister publication, _Channelnomics.eu_. [You can read Part One of the report in full here](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/feature/2408497/the-top-30-german-it-distributors-you-need-to-know-part-one "You can read Part One of the report in full here"). Undoubtedly one of the German channel's most striking quirks is the extent to which it is bossed by a trio of distribution goliaths in the form of Ingram Micro, Tech Data and ALSO, who boast combined estimated sales of nearly €11bn. Amanuel Dag, DACH country manager at analyst Context, said the power wielded by this triumvirate is closely linked to the market's highly price-sensitive nature. "The market is more consolidated here in Germany and therefore it's more price competitive than other countries," said Dag. "There's not much profit to make. The margins are always lower than one per cent for box-moving business around PCs, tablet and laptops; it's not a big secret that telecoms distributors are making more on laptop bags than the mobile PCs themselves. The saying ‘get big, get niche or get out' counts a lot for distribution in Germany - either they are big enough to survive or they find a niche with a higher margin." But it is perhaps precisely because Swiss ALSO and US broadline duo Tech Data and Ingram dominate so heavily that there exists below them a formidable pack of quirky home-grown heroes that have carved out a niche outside of box-shifting. _Channelnomics.eu_ began its [Focus in Germany season](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/special/2405808/focus-on-germany "Focus in Germany season") by counting down the country's top 50 resellers - or 'system houses'. Now it's the turn of the distributors, as _Channelnomics_ examines the country's top 30 IT wholesalers by revenue. Part One counts down numbers 20 to 21. Stay tuned for Parts Two and Three, which will review 20 to 11, and 10 to one, respectively. So here we go... **30) Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH - €47m** UK-based Wick Hill is one of Germany's leading security VADs, with local revenues in its fiscal 2014 of €46.7m, up 34 per cent on the previous year. Headquartered in Hamburg (_pictured_) and with 56 staff, [Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH](https://www.wickhill.de/ "Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH") counts WatchGuard, Kaspersky and Fortinet among its key vendors. **29) DELO Computer GmbH - €56m** Peripherals specialist [DELO](http://www.delo.com/ "DELO") saw sales dip by four per cent in 2013 to €56.4m, according to its most recent accounts. evidence.title: MD-NET - WMS
evidence.excerpt: [![WMS Logo](/uskur/punica_wms/img/wms-color.svg)](/) [![](/uskur/punica_wms/img/nmd-logo-small-updated.png) Official Journal](https://www.nmd-journal.com/ "Neuromuscular Disorders is the official journal of the World Muscle Society") * [Login](/login) * [Register](/register) ![](/image/c4bd28ce-31cb-4412-8f7b-a841354b0f9e?w=200&c=1 "MD-NET") # MD-NET MD-NET (Muscular Dystrophy Network) is a Germany-wide consortium funded by the BMBF to improve medical care for people with neuromuscular diseases (funding code 01GM0887). From 2003 up to and including 2013, extensive structures were created to promote basic research, diagnostics and the establishment of clinical studies. MD-NET bundles competences from all over Germany for the research of muscular dystrophies, spinal muscular atrophies (SMA), and other rare hereditary neuromuscular diseases. MD-NET has been constituted since 2006 as a non-profit association - MD-NET e.V. - in order to be able to act Europe-wide, and thus became the German partner of TREAT-NMD (Assessment and Treatment of Neuromuscular Diseases), a network of excellence for rare diseases funded by the EU in FP6. Within TREAT-NMD, MD-NET leads the activities on European harmonized patient registries, biobanks and a European Clinical Trial Center, thus enabling the translation of research results into clinical trials, and the transfer of results such as current treatment standards to the majority of muscular dystrophy patients in Germany. The goal is to establish new scientific knowledge on genetics, diagnostics and therapy of neuromuscular diseases and a comprehensive molecular diagnostics for the currently known gene loci in muscular dystrophies, spinal muscular atrophies and hereditary neuropathies, as well as linkage and mutation analyses for previously unknown genes. The network is supported by the MD-NET network center. It is located in the Friedrich-Baur-Institute at the Dept. of Neurology, Ludwig-Maximilians-University of Munich. evidence.excerpt: # L2.3 | Home and Office Networks: Beginner Guide Modem Router Switch Access Points and WiFi ## Vlad Romanov 14 likes ### Description 1894 views Posted: 25 Sep 2025 This session explains how a home or small office network actually works from the point where your internet service provider brings fiber or coax into the building through the modem the router and the switch and then out to wired devices and access points. We show how many consumer gateways combine these roles in one unit and when separate hardware makes sense. You will see how a physical layer switch lets you expand ports for desktops or other wired gear and how access points extend coverage so laptops and phones can roam while staying connected. We walk through what managed and unmanaged switches do at a practical level how devices obtain addresses and how traffic flows across the network. We also cover why a gigabit connection can still feel slow during peak use and how streaming video video calls and large file transfers share limited throughput. If you are preparing for OT topics this primer gives you the foundation to reason about topologies performance and reliability before you step into plant networks. Ihr gebuchtes Paket können Sie selbstverständlich jederzeit erweitern, sodass Ihr Internetauftritt gemeinsam mit Ihrem Unternehmen wachsen kann und immer Ihren jeweils aktuellen Ansprüchen genügt. evidence.excerpt: # Meet Germany's top 30 IT distributors #### Ingram, ALSO and Tech Data dominate but there's no shortage of local heroes in the German distribution market, according to our sister title Channelnomics Did you know that seven cents in every euro spent on ICT in Germany travels through just three giant IT distributors? That's one of the more surprising findings of research into the top 30 ICT distributors in Germany which has been carried out by our sister publication, _Channelnomics.eu_. [You can read Part One of the report in full here](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/feature/2408497/the-top-30-german-it-distributors-you-need-to-know-part-one "You can read Part One of the report in full here"). Undoubtedly one of the German channel's most striking quirks is the extent to which it is bossed by a trio of distribution goliaths in the form of Ingram Micro, Tech Data and ALSO, who boast combined estimated sales of nearly €11bn. Amanuel Dag, DACH country manager at analyst Context, said the power wielded by this triumvirate is closely linked to the market's highly price-sensitive nature. "The market is more consolidated here in Germany and therefore it's more price competitive than other countries," said Dag. "There's not much profit to make. The margins are always lower than one per cent for box-moving business around PCs, tablet and laptops; it's not a big secret that telecoms distributors are making more on laptop bags than the mobile PCs themselves. The saying ‘get big, get niche or get out' counts a lot for distribution in Germany - either they are big enough to survive or they find a niche with a higher margin." But it is perhaps precisely because Swiss ALSO and US broadline duo Tech Data and Ingram dominate so heavily that there exists below them a formidable pack of quirky home-grown heroes that have carved out a niche outside of box-shifting. _Channelnomics.eu_ began its [Focus in Germany season](http://www.channelnomics.eu/channelnomics-eu/special/2405808/focus-on-germany "Focus in Germany season") by counting down the country's top 50 resellers - or 'system houses'. Now it's the turn of the distributors, as _Channelnomics_ examines the country's top 30 IT wholesalers by revenue. Part One counts down numbers 20 to 21. Stay tuned for Parts Two and Three, which will review 20 to 11, and 10 to one, respectively. So here we go... **30) Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH - €47m** UK-based Wick Hill is one of Germany's leading security VADs, with local revenues in its fiscal 2014 of €46.7m, up 34 per cent on the previous year. Headquartered in Hamburg (_pictured_) and with 56 staff, [Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH](https://www.wickhill.de/ "Wick Hill Kommunikationstechnik GmbH") counts WatchGuard, Kaspersky and Fortinet among its key vendors. **29) DELO Computer GmbH - €56m** Peripherals specialist [DELO](http://www.delo.com/ "DELO") saw sales dip by four per cent in 2013 to €56.4m, according to its most recent accounts. findings.statement: The candidate entity is RHEIN IT, an IT-Systemhaus from Düsseldorf, Germany.
notes: Multiple official website pages consistently identify RHEIN IT as an IT-Systemhaus from Düsseldorf.

findings.statement: The company-owned website is https://www.rhein-it.de/.
notes: The submitted domain hosts official company pages that present RHEIN IT's services and company information.
Non-standard finding kind "official-website" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT has a Germany presence, headquartered in Düsseldorf.
notes: The official website states the company is based in Düsseldorf and serves the surrounding Düsseldorf, Ratingen, Mettmann, Neuss, Mönchengladbach, Krefeld, Duisburg, Köln and Niederrhein area.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT is active in network technology, IT infrastructure, and IT security services.
notes: The website lists Netzwerktechnik, IT-Sicherheit, server, workstation, and mobile workplace services as core areas.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT provides managed IT services including support, monitoring, maintenance, backup, update management, and hosting for business customers.
notes: The support page describes direct support, monitoring, system tests, remote maintenance, and ongoing infrastructure care; hosting and provider-change pages describe managed web and email services.
Non-standard finding kind "role-activity" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT performs system-house and system-integration work for IT infrastructures, including networking, servers, and workplace solutions.
notes: The homepage describes RHEIN IT as an IT-Systemhaus offering IT solutions from network/server to mobile workplace, and service pages describe configuration and deployment work.
Non-standard finding kind "role-activity" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT operates as a Distributor supplying downstream resellers or channel partners.
notes: The official website describes direct IT services to end-customer SMEs and professionals and does not describe supplying downstream resellers, dealers, or channel partners.
Non-standard finding kind "role-activity" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT is the same entity as Rheinmetall, Rhein International UG, or the Tracxn-listed property company 'Rhein'.
notes: These independent sources describe different entities: a defence technology group, a trading company in Duisburg, and a property sales/marketing company, respectively.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT is listed as a top German system integrator in independent directories.
notes: The clutch.co directory page lists system integration companies in Germany generally, but the supplied excerpt does not identify RHEIN IT among them.
Non-standard finding kind "role-activity" was normalized to other.

findings.statement: RHEIN IT is an authorised distributor for WLAN or networking hardware brands.
notes: Independent evidence about distributors such as AccessPoint, Purdicom, or Winncom does not mention RHEIN IT.
Non-standard finding kind "role-activity" was normalized to other.

reasons: The official website consistently presents RHEIN IT as an IT-Systemhaus offering managed services, support, monitoring, hosting, and IT infrastructure care.
